text.p: ZAGREB, April 7 (Zagreb) - Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Speaker of parliament (Sabor) Vlatko Pavletic returned from a five-day official visit from Japan. Opening of Japanese Embassy in Zagreb is expected very soon.

- United Nations Transitional Authority in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) will suspend some of its activities during elections set for April 13 for security reasons, UNTAES public relations office says in a statement.

- International Civil Aviation Organisation approved Croatia controlling its entire air space, even part southeast of disputed Prevlaka peninsula, despite efforts of Yugoslavia to prevent the decision.
- Poll conducted by Institute for Applied Social Research shows HDZ victory in elections is secured.
- After intense negotiations between Croatian and Yugoslav delegations an accord on dual citizenship has not been reached.

- Tourism Minister Niko Bulic predicts good season but also very cautious as Croatia faces fierce competition and still suffers from unnecessary drawbacks. Croatian wine, says Bulic, is still the most expensive in Mediterranean region.
